labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

items.body:
### Environment

- ChatGPT desktop app: 26.917.71314, build 10954, production channel. Its configured updater reported "up to date" on 25 September 2026.
- Bundle identifier: `com.openai.codex`.
- Bundled Codex Framework: 153.0.8010.53.
- macOS 27.0 (26A428), Apple Silicon (arm64), hardware model Mac15,13, 24 GB RAM.

### Problem

The desktop application terminates unexpectedly during ordinary use. macOS recorded **11 ChatGPT crash reports on 25 September 2026**. The latest crash occurred at **15:07:55 CEST**. The prior ten occurred at 01:54:34, 08:16:54, 08:21:05, 08:21:14, 10:17:31, 12:53:49, 13:12:56, 14:17:32, 14:39:47, and 14:49:31 CEST.

All 11 reports have the same native signature:

```text
Process: ChatGPT (com.openai.codex)
Exception: EXC_BREAKPOINT / SIGTRAP
Termination: SIGNAL 5 (Trace/BPT trap)
Faulting thread: thread 0, usually named CrBrowserMain
Codex Framework image UUID: 4c4c444f-5555-3144-a131-fae27cec809b
Top frame imageOffset: 165734432 (identical in all 11 reports)
Top frame symbolLocation: 35821868
ARM exception state: (Breakpoint) brk 0
```

The crash reporter labels the nearest exported symbol `node::inspector::protocol::BinaryValue::AppendSerialized`, but the very large `symbolLocation` means that label is **not reliable source-level attribution**. Vendor symbolication of the framework image offset is needed to identify the actual failing function.

The reports show an application `SIGTRAP`, rather than an OS Jetsam/`EXC_RESOURCE` termination. I reviewed the desktop logs around the five crashes from 12:53 to 14:49 and found no warning or error message common to all five immediately before termination. I do not have a deterministic reproduction step or evidence that a particular task, browser operation, model, or prompt triggers it.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Launch ChatGPT desktop 26.917.71314 on this Mac.
2. Use the app normally. The main process may terminate without an in-app error.
3. Reopen the app and continue working; the same crash can recur after minutes or hours.

### Expected behavior

The desktop app stays running and preserves the active workflow.

### What I checked

- macOS produced eleven separate crash reports with the identical top framework image offset.
- The app is currently up to date according to its configured updater.
- A high-CPU third-party Stream Deck plugin was removed earlier on 25 September. The same app crash signature occurred both before and after that removal, so the plugin is not sufficient to explain these crashes.
- High CPU and compressed memory were observed earlier in the day, but those measurements were **not captured at the crash moments**. They do not establish a memory or thermal cause.
- Related open reports: [#41618](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/41618) has a CrBrowserMain SIGTRAP on an older build, without a matching framework offset established; [#42333](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/42333) is a persistent startup freeze with high CPU, not a crash; [#38970](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/38970) reports a dispatch-thread soft limit crash in an older build. [#42317](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/42317) and [#43180](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/43180) are also related. None establishes that the underlying cause matches this build and signature.

### Request

Please symbolicate image offset `165734432` for Codex Framework 153.0.8010.53 / UUID `4c4c444f-5555-3144-a131-fae27cec809b`, investigate the repeated `CrBrowserMain` trap, and advise whether there is a confirmed workaround or fixed desktop build. I can provide a specifically requested, redacted crash excerpt through an appropriate private channel.

### What issue are you seeing?

On Windows x64, Codex 0.157.0 repeatedly opens unwanted console windows, including one titled:

C:\Users\<user>\.codex\packages\app-server-daemon\releases\0.157.0-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc\bin\codex-code-mode-host.exe

PowerShell command windows also appear during tool execution.

Reproduction:

Launch Codex 0.157.0: pop-ups appear.
Close and reopen Codex: pop-ups return.
Roll back to 0.156.0: pop-ups stop and commands work.
Upgrade back to 0.157.0: pop-ups return.

Expected: Internal helpers and noninteractive commands run without opening visible console windows.

Diagnostic detail: In the affected session, the helper ran under the managed app-server daemon and had a visible window. On 0.156.0, it ran directly under the CLI and had no visible window (MainWindowHandle = 0). This may implicate the daemon launch path.

Disabling code_mode_host did not resolve the reported pop-ups and disabled command execution, so that setting was reverted.

I like the updated UI and would prefer to stay on the latest version, but the recurring windows are disruptive.

No pop ups when I use CLI :(

### What issue are you seeing?

Codex CLI sometimes remains stuck in a working state indefinitely while processing a turn.

The model stops making visible progress, no new tokens are consumed, and no error is displayed. The process remains active and does not transition to a completed or failed state.

Typing additional characters or sending another message sometimes causes the interface to become responsive again. The previous turn may then continue.

The issue occurs across multiple independent Codex workspaces and agents. It is more frequent in some workspaces than others, but it is not isolated to a single workspace.

The issue occurs with all tested models, including GPT-6, GPT-5.6, and GPT-5.5, through the relay API provider.

The issue occurred before I started using Herdr, so Herdr does not appear to be the sole cause.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Start Codex CLI in PowerShell 7.6.6 on Windows.
2. Configure Codex to use a third-party OpenAI-compatible relay API provider.
3. Start a normal coding task that requires one or more model turns.
4. Allow the task to continue until Codex sends a request.
5. In some cases, Codex remains in a working state without visible progress.
6. Wait several minutes. The process remains active, no new tokens are consumed, and no error is shown.
7. Type additional input or send another message.
8. The interface may become responsive again and the previous operation may continue.

### What is the expected behavior?

Codex CLI should enforce a finite timeout while waiting for the initial HTTP response.

If the provider does not return an initial response within the timeout, Codex should:

1. Cancel the request.
2. Report a clear timeout or connection error.
3. Enter the existing retry or failure path.
4. Keep the terminal UI responsive.
5. Avoid requiring additional keyboard input to resume progress.

### Additional information

The relay endpoints used during testing were:

- https://cf.api.fan
- https://slb-v1.api.fan

Observed log messages include:

- Temporary capacity limit
- 429 Too Many Requests
- Connection failed

The logs show very long delays between request creation and receipt of the initial HTTP response headers. Observed delays include approximately 105, 287, 409, and 615 seconds.

The configured stream idle timeout does not appear to cover this failure mode because it starts after the HTTP response headers have already been received. The apparent hang occurs while waiting for the initial response headers.

The issue appears to occur before response body streaming begins.

Switching between the CF endpoint and the SLB endpoint did not reliably resolve the issue.

The problem is more frequent in some workspaces, including a workspace named "BV-DiLiBlay", but it is not limited to that workspace.

The behavior is intermittent and cannot be reproduced on every request.


After this error the session is stuck — no further progress is possible because compaction never succeeds, so the context remains over the limit.

### What is the expected behavior?

Two parts:

1. **Compaction support for Kimi K3 on Bedrock.** Since #36981 enabled v1 remote compaction for Amazon Bedrock providers, compaction requests for Bedrock models go through the remote compact endpoint — but `global.moonshotai.kimi-k3` is rejected by that endpoint with a `validation_error`. Please enable compaction for Kimi K3 (and other non-Anthropic/non-OpenAI models available on Bedrock) so that long-running sessions can compact normally.

2. **Graceful fallback instead of a hard stop.** If the remote compact endpoint rejects the configured model, Codex should fall back to local compaction (or surface a recoverable error that lets the user switch models / start a new thread with context) rather than leaving the thread permanently wedged. Today the only workaround is to abandon the session.

### Related issues

- #37010 — Support configuring `remote_compaction` per model (would let users control this behavior)
- #45393 — Resume/handoff to third-party Responses providers fails: item type "compaction" is not supported
- #36981 — Enable remote compaction for Amazon Bedrock (introduced the v1 remote compaction path for Bedrock)

### Additional information

The error is emitted from the remote compaction path (`codex-rs/core/src/compact_remote_v2.rs` / `session/turn.rs`). The `validation_error` code suggests the compact endpoint validates the model name and only allows a fixed set of models. Since Bedrock hosts many third-party models (Kimi, DeepSeek, Qwen, etc.), it would be helpful if either the endpoint supported compaction for these models or Codex degraded gracefully when it does not.

Optional node_repl warning: CODEX_WINDOWS_REGISTERED_CORE unset.

Expected: connectors initialize and tools are callable.
Actual: initialization fails and connector tools are unavailable.

The timing suggests a regression; causation is unconfirmed.
Feedback session IDs: `01a0d88a-6f14-7fa3-81d1-454f2b3bd364` and `01a0d9b6-04e7-72f1-a80f-cb9902d07826`.
## Additional evidence consolidated from #48154

After reset, Gmail tools appeared in the tool catalogue, but runtime inspection returned `undefined` and calling `tools.mcp__codex_apps__gmail_get_profile({})` failed with `TypeError: tools.mcp__codex_apps__gmail_get_profile is not a function`. `gmail_list_labels` also failed. These calls failed before connector dispatch or Gmail authentication.

### Startup-grace test

Added top-level `mcp_optional_startup_grace_ms = 0` to the user config, backed up the original, and fully quit and reopened Codex. The problem persisted:
- First execution cell: profile and labels tools appeared in `ALL_TOOLS`, with runtime type `function`.
- Next execution cell: the profile invocation failed with the same TypeError.
- A subsequent cell checked and invoked together: the profile entry was absent from `ALL_TOOLS`, its runtime type was `undefined`, and invocation failed.

The setting remains enabled. The two feedback submissions above predate this startup test. The observed sequence does not independently prove that initialization failure caused registry invalidation; please correlate the logs.

### Integration configuration

No user `[mcp_servers.codex_apps]` configuration was found; this project's `.codex/config.toml` does not exist. The explicitly configured MCP servers are `node_repl` and `cua_repl`. Gmail plugin version `0.1.10` declares `apps: ./.app.json` with a required Gmail app connector. Its manifest does not declare `mcpServers`, and no `.mcp.json` was found in that plugin cache. This identifies Gmail as a plugin-provided app connector exposed through `codex_apps`, rather than a manually configured `codex_apps` server; it does not establish that the Gmail plugin itself launches a standalone MCP server.

Duplicate #48154 is being closed to keep follow-up in this original issue. Its detailed diagnostic comment remains available at https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/48154#issuecomment-5837250809.

## Why

Large shell snapshots need a replay path that does not add their state to the child process environment.

## What changed

- Probe descriptor-path access inside the capture sandbox. Retain environment replay for `sh` and when descriptor paths are unavailable; use normal shell startup if preparing the replay file fails.
- Group options and aliases during capture so sourcing preserves their parsing behavior.

## Testing

Add coverage for concurrent replays with 480 KiB payloads, pipe and TTY execution, stdin preservation, descriptor cleanup, sandbox protection, blocked descriptor-path fallback, and alias/option parsing equivalence.

### What version of Codex CLI is running?

`codex-cli 0.155.0-alpha.16.3`, bundled with VS Code extension `openai.chatgpt-26.917.62051-darwin-arm64`.  The source trace below is pinned to `4b1c0c30dabd08fed7d6523844f9156d982eb297`.

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT Enterprise

### Which model were you using?

gpt-6-sol

### What platform is your computer?

`Darwin 25.6.0 arm64 arm` (`uname -mprs`).

### What terminal emulator and version are you using (if applicable)?

VS Code extension. The terminal emulator version was not recorded.

### Codex doctor report

```json
Not captured for the extension-bundled binary.
```

### What issue are you seeing?

A Bash `PermissionRequest` hook can approve or deny an `exec_command` escalation, but its input omits the selected execution directory and environment. For commands with relative paths, the hook cannot determine which directory an approval would affect.

At the pinned revision, `exec_command` [resolves `workdir` against the selected environment](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/4b1c0c30dabd08fed7d6523844f9156d982eb297/codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers/unified_exec/exec_command.rs#L186-L205). The resulting [`ApprovalAction::ExecCommand` retains `cwd` and `environment_id`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/4b1c0c30dabd08fed7d6523844f9156d982eb297/codex-rs/core/src/tools/approvals.rs#L65-L80). Its [PermissionRequest projection passes only the command and justification](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/4b1c0c30dabd08fed7d6523844f9156d982eb297/codex-rs/core/src/tools/approvals.rs#L166-L173) to a [serializer that emits `command` and optional `description`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/4b1c0c30dabd08fed7d6523844f9156d982eb297/codex-rs/core/src/tools/sandboxing.rs#L128-L149).

The top-level hook `cwd` cannot supply the missing context. Codex [sets it from the host-local hook directory](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/4b1c0c30dabd08fed7d6523844f9156d982eb297/codex-rs/core/src/hook_runtime.rs#L247-L277), and the [Hooks documentation](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/hooks#common-input-fields) defines it as the session working directory. This is a missing permission-payload capability, not a claim that the documented `cwd` value regressed.

A policy that denies unknown directories rejects a valid approval for another worktree. A policy that treats top-level `cwd` as the command directory can approve an operation in the wrong location. This report does not claim that hooks replace Codex's sandbox.


### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Create `/tmp/codex-hook-cwd/a` and `/tmp/codex-hook-cwd/b`. Start Codex with the session directory set to `a`.
2. In a disposable Codex home, configure and trust a `PermissionRequest` command hook with matcher `^Bash$`. Have it append its stdin JSON to a file and return no decision, so the normal approval prompt remains in control.
3. Use `on-request` approval and a read-only permission profile. Invoke `exec_command` with arguments equivalent to:

```json
{
  "cmd": "pwd",
  "workdir": "/tmp/codex-hook-cwd/b",
  "sandbox_permissions": "require_escalated",
  "justification": "check permission hook context"
}
```

4. Repeat with the same command and justification, but set `workdir` to `/tmp/codex-hook-cwd/a`.
5. Compare each hook event's `cwd` and `tool_input`. If the requests are approved, compare the two `pwd` outputs.

The pinned repository has an [integration test that invokes a real Bash PermissionRequest hook](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/4b1c0c30dabd08fed7d6523844f9156d982eb297/codex-rs/core/tests/suite/hooks.rs#L3285-L3352). Giving that test two workdirs and checking the recorded hook input would make this a deterministic regression test. The PermissionRequest omission reported here follows from the pinned producer code; I have not captured this specific event from the installed binary.


### What is the expected behavior?

`PermissionRequest` should expose the pending command's resolved execution directory and selected environment identity in explicit fields. A relative `workdir` must resolve using the selected environment's path semantics.

Keep top-level `cwd` as the host-local session or hook directory. Keep the existing allow, deny, and normal approval behavior.

The same [approval projection](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/4b1c0c30dabd08fed7d6523844f9156d982eb297/codex-rs/core/src/tools/approvals.rs#L198-L224) also drops retained context for `Execve` and managed-network Bash requests. Those sibling routes should expose the context available for their own pending operation.


### Additional information

A separate live `PreToolUse` probe on the installed binary supplied an explicit workdir. The command ran there, but the captured hook input contained only `tool_input.command` and the session `cwd`. This supports the related reports below. The PermissionRequest finding above is based on the pinned source and its existing integration path.

I have a [candidate branch](https://github.com/BridgeAR/codex/tree/BridgeAR/2026-09-25-codex-hook-workdir), based on `4b1c0c30`, with the implementation in [commit `9b31c45e`](https://github.com/BridgeAR/codex/commit/9b31c45e94ff2df2859ca1fc4a7107250b7cc305). It could serve as a base for a maintainer fix. The patch carries the selected execution directory and environment identity through:

- `PreToolUse` for unified `exec_command`;
- applicable Bash `PermissionRequest` paths;
- immediate `PostToolUse` completion; and
- terminal `PostToolUse` completion after `write_stdin`.

It may help resolve the unified-exec portions of these existing reports:

- [#33986](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/33986): `exec_command` `PreToolUse` loses per-call `workdir`.
- [#32360](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/32360): `PreToolUse` reports the session directory instead of the execution directory.
- [#37251](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/37251): `PreToolUse` omits the effective directory for shell-like tools.
- [#40348](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/40348): `PreToolUse` and `PostToolUse` need the effective directory, including delayed completion.

The branch does not change classic `shell_command`, which #32360 and #37251 also cover. Code-mode execution could not be verified on this macOS ARM64 host because its `rusty_v8` build artifact was unavailable. Windows and remote execution remain unverified. On the preceding main revision, 105 focused host tests passed; the patch stayed byte-identical when moved to `4b1c0c30`. `just clippy -p codex-core` and `just fmt-check` passed on `4b1c0c30`. The broader `codex-core` suite was not all green, so this branch is a candidate base rather than a completed upstream validation.

    or nested mount before starting the sandbox

`/mnt/wslg/distro` is WSLg's standard read-only alias of the distro root.

After manually unmounting `/mnt/wslg/distro`, the sandbox worked immediately,
including workspace file creation and Git commands.

items.title: Deduplicate retained instructions across Guardian reviews
items.body:
Deduplicate retained instructions across Guardian reviews

## Why

Reused Guardian sessions already contain previously delivered instructions. Follow-up reviews can avoid repeating that evidence, but must deliver it again if it changes or compaction removes it.

## What changed

- Track retained source identity, revision, and completeness in host-owned history metadata, preserving revisions during replay.
- Omit retained instructions from synchronous review inputs only when the same complete revision remains in reviewer history.
- Restore missing evidence after reviewer compaction, enforcing the request budget before persisting additions. Classify restored evidence as context rather than new user authorization.
- Keep source-order labels stable across eviction and retain full delivery for legacy records without reliable provenance.

## Testing

Add coverage for consecutive-review deduplication, changed revisions, missing or incomplete metadata, and restoring compacted evidence exactly once. Extend compaction and resume coverage to verify retained revisions.

Terminal windows repeatedly pop up while Codex is being used.

Desktop (Windows/MSIX): UI stays English after selecting 中文 — enable_i18n never loads because Statsig init fails with EXDEV rename error## Environment
- App: Codex Desktop, version 26.917.9434.0
- Install: Microsoft Store (MSIX)
  C:\Program Files\WindowsApps\OpenAI.Codex_26.917.9434.0_x64__2p2nqsd0c76g0
- OS: Windows 11 26H1 (build 28000)

## Summary
Selecting "Settings → General → Language → 中文（中国）" saves
localeOverride = "zh-CN", but the UI stays in English after a full restart.
The language dropdown shows 中文 as selected, yet nothing is localized.

## What I found

1. The setting IS saved correctly:
   ~/.codex/config.toml
   [desktop]
   localeOverride = "zh-CN"

2. On every launch the app fails to initialize its Statsig feature-gate system:

   warning [global-state] Failed to persist global state
     errorCode=EXDEV  errorMessage="EXDEV: cross-device link not permitted,
     rename '...\Codex\web\Codex\.statsig-state.json.tmp-...'
         -> '...\Codex\web\Codex\statsig-state.json'"

   warning [electron-message-handler] Failed to initialize host Statsig identity
     errorMessage="EXDEV: cross-device link not permitted, ..."

   info browser_use_availability_resolved available=false reason=statsig-disabled

3. The app-data dirs are MSIX junctions:
   C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Roaming\Codex
     -> C:\WpSystem\S-1-5-21-...\LocalCache\Roaming\Codex
   C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\Codex
     -> C:\WpSystem\S-1-5-21-...\LocalCache\Local\Codex

4. In app.asar, the locale provider and the language picker read the same
   enable_i18n gate (id 72216192) with DIFFERENT defaults:
   - Intl provider:    gate.get('enable_i18n', false)
     -> when Statsig is unavailable, messages stays undefined and the UI
        falls back to the default (English).
   - Language picker:  gate.get('enable_i18n', true)
     -> the picker still renders and accepts a selection.

   So with Statsig disabled, the picker is visible but localization never
   loads — exactly the observed behavior.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Install Codex Desktop from the Microsoft Store.
2. Open Settings → General → Language and choose 中文（中国）.
3. Fully quit and relaunch Codex.
4. The dropdown shows 中文, but the whole UI stays in English.

## Expected
The UI renders in the selected language.

## Actual
The UI stays in English.

## Notes
The EXDEV rename failure appears tied to the MSIX write-redirection (the
app-data path is a junction into C:\WpSystem), so the Statsig state can
never persist and gate evaluation always falls back to code defaults.

items.title: TUI: make pasted text an atomic composer element so multiline `/goal` input survives Windows paste + slash dispatch

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: TUI
labels.description: Issues related to the terminal user interface: text input, menus and dialogs, and terminal display

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

items.body:
## Summary

On native Windows, multiline/large pasted text can cross the boundary between **composer display state**, **slash-command parsing**, and **Goal persistence** in inconsistent ways.

A common workflow is:

```text
/goal <paste a long multi-paragraph task brief here>
```

The user expects the pasted brief to remain one atomic argument to `/goal`. In practice, Windows paste delivery can cause only the first line/prefix to be consumed as the command while the remainder becomes ordinary composer input / a queued steer. For large pastes, Codex also uses `[Pasted Content N chars]` + `pending_pastes`, but different paths inspect either the visible placeholder text, the expanded text, or materialized paste files.

This makes it hard for the user to know whether a long pasted brief is actually part of the active Goal or merely later conversational context.

## Observed user-facing failure

On Windows Terminal / PowerShell, a long multiline brief pasted after `/goal` can result in a state like:

```text
Goal active
Objective: 执行他说的这些：
```

while the remainder of the pasted brief appears separately under a pending/queued message area.

That is semantically different from the intended result:

```text
Goal active
Objective: 执行他说的这些：
  <entire pasted multi-paragraph brief>
```

The remainder may still reach the model as normal context/steering, but it no longer has Goal lifecycle semantics.

## This overlaps several existing reports, but the missing invariant is broader

Related:

- #31416 — multiline paste on Windows submits the first line immediately and leaves the remainder in the input box.
- #26025 — `/goal edit` used to stop at a pasted newline on Windows (closed/fixed).
- #44075 — `/goal` materializes paste placeholders into inline file instructions that `/goal edit` does not reconstruct.
- #22616 — large pasted `/goal ...` can bypass the slash-command path when the visible composer contains only a paste placeholder.
- #24304 — request for a compact large-paste attachment/document UX.
- #44490 — pasted control characters can still be interpreted as composer shortcuts when paste arrives as key events rather than one paste event.

The common issue is that a paste is not treated as one canonical structured/atomic composer element through **all** input and dispatch paths.

## Reference implementation: Oh My Pi

Oh My Pi already implements a useful model for this.

### 1. Buffer bracketed paste as one payload

`packages/tui/src/bracketed-paste.ts`

It buffers `ESC[200~ ... ESC[201~` across chunks and only emits a complete paste payload once the end marker is received (with safety limits for broken/truncated paste streams).

https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/blob/main/packages/tui/src/bracketed-paste.ts

### 2. Store large paste payload separately and insert an atomic marker

`packages/tui/src/components/editor.ts`

For >10 lines or >1000 chars, OMP stores the exact payload in an internal paste map and inserts a compact marker such as:

```text
[Paste #2, +30 lines]
```

The marker can live inline with ordinary text, e.g.:

```text
/command prefix [Paste #2, +30 lines] suffix
```

The editor also treats paste/image tokens as atomic during deletion/editing, so the user cannot accidentally leave a half-corrupted placeholder.

https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/blob/main/packages/tui/src/components/editor.ts

### 3. Expand before dispatch

The same editor exposes `getExpandedText()`, which replaces the marker with the exact stored payload. Its submit path expands before handing the final text to the host.

OMP's coding-agent paths then parse/execute slash commands from the expanded submission text rather than using the display marker as the semantic source.

There is also a regression test specifically ensuring queued/follow-up submissions expand `[Paste #N]` before dispatch:

https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/blob/main/packages/coding-agent/test/input-controller-followup-paste-expansion.test.ts

### 4. Very large paste UX is layered on top of the same primitive

OMP also exposes an `onLargePaste` hook that can offer:

- attach as a wrapped block,
- save to a file and reference it,
- paste inline,

without changing the core invariant that the original payload remains associated with one paste object.

https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/blob/main/packages/coding-agent/src/modes/controllers/input-controller.ts

## Suggested invariant for Codex

Regardless of terminal transport, paste size, slash command, or whether the agent is currently streaming:

> **One physical paste should become one structured composer element whose exact payload is preserved, editable as one unit, and expanded through one canonical API before semantic command dispatch.**

In other words, command parsing should not depend on whether the current UI representation happens to be literal multiline text, `[Pasted Content N chars]`, or a materialized paste file.

## Possible implementation direction

Codex already has most of the raw ingredients (`pending_pastes`, paste placeholders, `Event::Paste`, Goal materialization). The minimal architectural improvement could be:

1. Represent paste spans as structured/atomic draft elements rather than relying on display text as the command parser's source of truth.
2. Provide one canonical `expanded_text()` / semantic-text view for dispatch.
3. Run slash-command recognition and argument extraction against that semantic view.
4. Keep display placeholders compact, but make edits/deletes operate on the whole paste element.
5. Ensure the Windows fallback/paste-burst path accumulates the entire physical paste before Enter/Tab/etc. can be interpreted as normal composer actions.
6. Reuse the same semantic expansion for normal submit, steer/follow-up, `/goal`, and `/goal edit`.
7. If Goal persistence must externalize a long objective, externalize/reconstruct the **whole semantic objective**, not transport-specific paste chunks.

This does not require copying OMP code; the useful part is the invariant and separation between **display representation** and **semantic submission text**.

## Reproduction to cover

Windows Terminal + PowerShell:

1. Start Codex TUI.
2. Type:
   ```text
   /goal 执行下面完整任务：
   ```
3. Paste a multi-paragraph CJK task brief with bullets and blank lines.
4. Press Enter once.
5. Inspect the active Goal and pending composer/steer state.

### Expected

- Nothing submits during the paste.
- The full pasted brief remains one editable composer object.
- Pressing Enter once dispatches one `/goal` invocation.
- The complete semantic payload is associated with that Goal (subject to explicit Goal-size normalization/materialization rules).
- No tail of the physical paste becomes an unrelated queued user message.

### Actual

On affected Windows paths, only the first line/prefix may become the Goal while the remaining pasted text is left/queued separately (see #31416 class of behavior).

## Acceptance tests

It would be useful to add regression coverage for:

- `/goal <multiline paste>` on Windows paste-event fallback.
- CJK first line + multiline body.
- Paste larger than the large-paste threshold.
- `/goal prefix <large paste> suffix`.
- paste + Enter arriving in the same terminal read.
- paste + Tab arriving in the same terminal read.
- submit while streaming / queued steer.
- edit/delete of a paste placeholder as one atomic unit.
- save → `/goal edit` round trip preserving semantic text.
- multiple paste blocks inside one Goal.

The main UX goal is simple: a user should be able to paste a long structured brief into `/goal` with the same confidence as pasting it into a normal modern editor, without needing to reason about terminal chunking or placeholder implementation details.

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using?

Two versions are installed simultaneously:

- `/Applications/Codex.app`: desktop `26.820.60940` (build `7119`), bundled CLI `0.150.0-alpha.8`
- `/Applications/ChatGPT.app`: desktop `26.917.71314` (build `10954`), bundled CLI `0.155.0-alpha.16.4`

Both bundles report:

```
CFBundleIdentifier: com.openai.codex
CFBundleDisplayName: ChatGPT
CFBundleName: ChatGPT
```

### What platform is your computer?

macOS, Apple Silicon.

### What issue are you seeing?

The Codex/ChatGPT migration can leave both `Codex.app` and `ChatGPT.app` installed with the same bundle identifier. macOS can then launch the older `/Applications/Codex.app` copy from an existing Dock/Applications shortcut.

This is not only a duplicate icon/storage problem. The older app launches an older bundled app-server runtime and exposes a reduced model catalog. In this observed state, GPT-6 models disappeared from the model picker even though the user's config still explicitly selected:

```toml
model = "gpt-6-sol"
```

The two bundled CLIs return different model catalogs for the same account and machine:

```console
$ /Applications/Codex.app/Contents/Resources/codex debug models
gpt-5.6-sol
gpt-5.6-terra
gpt-5.6-luna

$ /Applications/ChatGPT.app/Contents/Resources/codex debug models
gpt-6-astra
gpt-6-sol
gpt-6-luna
gpt-5.6-sol
gpt-5.6-terra
gpt-5.6-luna
```

Process inspection confirmed that the currently visible desktop window was running from:

```
/Applications/Codex.app/Contents/MacOS/ChatGPT
```

There is no reasonable way for a normal user to know that the visually identical shortcut launches a stale copy. The visible symptom is simply that models that worked previously have disappeared.

The duplicate-install mechanism appears related to #31944, but this report documents the additional user-facing model-catalog impact.

### Steps to reproduce the bug

1. Reach the migration state where both `/Applications/Codex.app` and `/Applications/ChatGPT.app` exist with bundle ID `com.openai.codex`.
2. Ensure the bundles contain different Codex runtime versions.
3. Launch Codex using the older existing shortcut/path, which resolves to `/Applications/Codex.app`.
4. Open the model picker.
5. Observe that GPT-6 models are absent.
6. Quit and launch `/Applications/ChatGPT.app`.
7. Open the model picker again.
8. Observe that GPT-6 Astra, Sol, and Luna are available.

The difference can also be verified with `codex debug models` using each bundle's embedded CLI, as shown above.

### What is the expected behavior?

The updater/installer should leave exactly one canonical application bundle, migrate Dock/LaunchServices shortcuts to it, and remove or clearly deprecate the stale bundle.

If two bundles with the same identifier are detected, the app should:

- launch the newest installed version;
- warn the user about the stale duplicate;
- avoid allowing an old runtime to silently replace the current model catalog;
- provide a safe cleanup/migration action.

A routine install or update must not leave two visually indistinguishable entry points where one silently hides current models.

### Additional information

- `codex doctor` can make diagnosis more confusing: it may report the newer desktop version discovered by bundle identifier while the running process actually comes from the older `/Applications/Codex.app` path.
- Computer Use also reports the bundle identifier as ambiguous because both application paths share `com.openai.codex`.
- Related: #31944, #31866, #32022.
- Posted at the affected user's request after verifying both bundle metadata, running process path, bundled CLI versions, and model catalogs.

labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

labels.name: app-server
labels.description: Issues involving app server protocol or interfaces

items.body:
### What issue are you seeing?

Hi! After updating `openai-codex` from `0.156.1-1` to `0.157.0-1` with pacman on Arch Linux, just running `codex` no longer opens a usable session:

```text
Error: this CLI has no complete local package; install a packaged Codex CLI or use the standalone installer
To work without the background server, rerun the same command with --no-daemon (including resume or fork and its arguments).
```

I had recently restored a Timeshift snapshot, so at first I thought I'd broken something locally. But the same error reproduces with a fresh `CODEX_HOME`, and `pacman -Qkk openai-codex` reports `15 total files, 0 altered files`.

`codex --no-daemon` works around it. It looks related to daemon auto-start becoming the default in 0.157.0.

### Environment

- Codex: `codex-cli 0.157.0`, Arch package `openai-codex 0.157.0-1`
- OS: Arch Linux x86_64, kernel `7.2.6-zen2-1-zen`
- Terminal: Ghostty 1.3.1-arch2; also reproduced in a separate PTY without a multiplexer
- Model/subscription: the minimal reproduction below needs neither authentication nor a model request

### Reproduction

With the Arch package installed:

```sh
repro_home=$(mktemp -d "$HOME/cdx-repro.XXXXXX")
CODEX_HOME="$repro_home" /usr/bin/codex app-server daemon start
```

This exits with code 1 and the package error above. A short home path matters here because a sufficiently long one hits a separate Unix socket path-length limit.

The user-facing regression is that an ordinary interactive `codex` launch now takes this failing path by default.

### What was checked

To rule out my existing setup, these tests used separate `CODEX_HOME` directories on the same machine:

| Test | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Arch 0.156.1, default interactive launch | Opens the input prompt |
| Arch 0.157.0, default interactive launch | Exits with the package error |
| Arch 0.157.0 with `--no-daemon` | Opens the input prompt |
| Arch 0.157.0 with `--disable daemon_auto_start` | Opens the input prompt |
| Arch 0.157.0, explicit daemon start | Same package error |
| Official 0.157.0 **complete package**, daemon start | Starts successfully, reports server version 0.157.0 |
| The exact same official executable copied out of that package, daemon start | Same package error |

The interactive tests used a dummy API key and a trust entry for the test directory to skip onboarding; no prompt was sent. The successful daemon was stopped after testing.

Both the complete `codex-package-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.zst` asset and the separate `codex-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.zst` asset were checked against their GitHub SHA-256 digests. The standalone binary decompresses to exactly the same executable used in the last test.

### Possible cause

The [Arch PKGBUILD](https://gitlab.archlinux.org/archlinux/packaging/packages/openai-codex/-/blob/0.157.0-1/PKGBUILD) installs the executables into `/usr/bin` and uses system dependencies. It doesn't install `codex-package.json` or the bundled `codex-path` / `codex-resources` layout that the official complete package has.

Looking at the tagged source:

- `daemon_auto_start` changed from [default false in 0.156.1](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.156.1/codex-rs/features/src/lib.rs#L937) to [default true in 0.157.0](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.157.0/codex-rs/features/src/lib.rs#L940).
- [Package detection](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.157.0/codex-rs/install-context/src/lib.rs#L286) needs `codex-package.json` next to the `bin` directory.
- [Daemon installation](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.157.0/codex-rs/app-server-daemon/src/prepare_install.rs#L146) returns this error when there is no recognized source package and no existing daemon installation to use.

I'm not sure how much of this should be fixed upstream versus in Arch's packaging. Could automatic startup fall back to the embedded server when the complete package layout isn't available? Explicitly starting the daemon could still report the missing requirements. If downstream packages need a new layout, some guidance for packagers would also help.

For now, this gets normal interactive use working again:

```sh
codex features disable daemon_auto_start
```

Thanks for taking a look. I found #47990 while searching, but that seems to be an npm dependency publishing issue rather than this native package startup failure.

### Codex doctor report

The relevant part of `codex doctor --json` from an isolated, credential-free home is below. Interestingly, the install check passes. Other checks are omitted here; missing authentication in that environment is intentional.

```json
{
  "codexVersion": "0.157.0",
  "installation": {
    "status": "ok",
    "summary": "installation looks consistent",
    "details": {
      "current executable": "/usr/bin/codex",
      "install context": "other",
      "managed package root": "not set"
    }
  }
}
```

### Product / use case
Codex Desktop, used for sustained, multi-file development and refactoring (ChatGPT Plus; September 2026). This is user-experience feedback rather than a claim of a measured tokenizer or billing defect.

### Problem
In long-running coding sessions, Codex's context-management behavior feels unnecessarily token-intensive. Repeatedly carrying large conversation histories, re-reading project material, and rebuilding context around compaction can consume substantial available context/usage without proportional progress on the coding task. This makes working on a long-lived codebase frustrating and reduces predictability when deciding whether to continue a thread or start over.

The concern is distinct from a request for a larger context window: **a larger window does not solve inefficient selection, retention, or reuse of relevant context.**

### Requested improvements
1. Keep a compact, durable record of current task state, accepted architectural decisions, constraints, files changed, and outstanding checks across compactions. Avoid making the agent reconstruct the same facts repeatedly.
2. Prefer targeted retrieval of changed or relevant files over repeatedly re-reading the whole repository or carrying stale tool output.
3. Improve visibility into **actual context occupancy vs. billed tokens vs. cache hits vs. compaction overhead** so users can tell where tokens go.
4. Offer transparent or configurable context/compaction controls appropriate for very long coding sessions, without silently losing critical constraints.
5. Provide a reliable handoff/checkpoint mechanism to start a fresh session while preserving verified project/task state, rather than relying on an opaque compressed chat transcript.

### Expected outcome
Long-running development tasks remain coherent and efficient, with less duplicated context and less rework after compaction. Please consider this alongside related specific reports such as #45296 (historical messages retained after compaction) and #11907 (cross-surface refresh).

No exact token measurements, trace, or app version are attached; these are recurring user observations and product requests, not independently verified root causes.

items.title: [otel] OTLP exporter headers must be a plaintext secret in config — add a headers helper command so the token can live in an OS keychain

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

labels.description: Issues involving config.toml, config keys, config merging, or config updates

items.body:
### What variant of Codex are you using?

App, CLI

### What feature would you like to see?

`[otel]` exporter headers are static strings, so exporting to an authenticated OTLP collector requires writing a bearer token in cleartext into a config file. For a managed deployment that file is root-owned and world-readable (mode 644), so every local user and process on the device can read a credential that is valid from anywhere.

There is currently no supported way to avoid this. Verified against the source at `4b1c0c3`, the value is passed through untouched at all three layers:

1. [`OtelExporterKind::OtlpHttp`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/4b1c0c30dabd08fed7d6523844f9156d982eb297/codex-rs/config/src/types.rs#L576-L594) declares `headers: HashMap<String, String>` and is `deny_unknown_fields`, so no alternative header source can be configured.
2. [`otel_init.rs`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/4b1c0c30dabd08fed7d6523844f9156d982eb297/codex-rs/core/src/otel_init.rs#L38-L42) copies them verbatim: `.map(|(k, v)| (k.clone(), v.clone()))`.
3. [`build_header_map`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/4b1c0c30dabd08fed7d6523844f9156d982eb297/codex-rs/otel/src/otlp.rs#L22-L32) passes each value straight to `HeaderValue::from_str`.

The only `env::var` call in the otel module is for `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TIMEOUT`, and there is no `${VAR}` interpolation during config loading.

This is worth calling out because the [config reference](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/config-file/config-reference) documents the feature with an example that reads as though env substitution works:

```toml
[otel]
exporter = { otlp-http = {
  endpoint = "https://otel.example.com/v1/logs",
  protocol = "binary",
  headers = { "x-otlp-api-key" = "${OTLP_TOKEN}" }
}}
```

Following that example sends the literal nine-character string `${OTLP_TOKEN}` as the header value and the collector rejects the request. Either the docs should drop the `${...}` notation, or — preferably — the substitution should be made real.

### Request

Add a way to resolve exporter headers at runtime from an external command, so the secret never has to be written to disk. Something equivalent to Claude Code's `otelHeadersHelper`: Codex invokes a configured command, the command returns the headers, and the secret stays in the OS keychain (`security find-generic-password` on macOS, Credential Manager on Windows, `secret-tool` on Linux).

```toml
[otel.exporter.otlp-http]
endpoint = "https://otel.example.com/v1/logs"
protocol = "binary"
headers-command = "/usr/local/bin/otel-headers"
```

A narrower version would also solve it: support `env-headers` alongside `headers`, mirroring the `env_http_headers` mechanism that `model_providers` already has. A helper command is preferable, because environment variables for GUI applications on macOS have to be set with `launchctl setenv`, which makes them readable by every process of that user — no better than the file.

`[otel.exporter.<id>.tls.*]` already supports mTLS, but it does not cover this case well: those fields take file paths, whereas MDM on macOS installs client identities into the keychain rather than as PEM files, so the private key ends up on disk anyway.

Related: #16248 asks for `[otel]` as cloud-managed defaults in the admin console, which would also remove the secret from the device — complementary rather than a duplicate, since that issue is about where config is authored and this one is about how the credential is resolved. #46458 covers a related constraint on the mTLS path.

### Additional information

_No response_

### What version of Codex CLI is running?

### What subscription do you have?

### Which model were you using?

Not relevant; the problem is in the TUI composer.

### What platform is your computer?

Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS, `Linux 6.17.0-122035-tuxedo x86_64 x86_64`, Wayland (`XDG_SESSION_TYPE=wayland`).

### What terminal emulator and version are you using?

[`shitty`](https://github.com/pg83/shitty), standalone Wayland terminal, release [15](https://github.com/pg83/shitty/releases/tag/15) (`st-linux-x86_64.tar.gz`). A local script named `st` launches the installed binary. No tmux or other multiplexer in the affected session.

### Codex doctor report

Not attached; the report was not needed to identify the terminal input path.

### What issue are you seeing?

After updating to 0.157.0, middle-clicking to paste the Wayland primary selection into the Codex CLI composer no longer inserts text. The user reports that `shitty` was unchanged and this worked before updating Codex to 0.157.0. This is distinct from Ctrl+V or clipboard paste.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. On Wayland in `shitty`, select text so it is available as the primary selection.
2. Start `codex` 0.157.0 with its default TUI settings in a terminal supporting middle-click paste.
3. Middle-click inside the composer.

The report comes from an interactive user session; I could inspect the configuration and source, but could not automate a physical middle-click reproduction or run a controlled 0.156.1 comparison.

### What is the expected behavior?

The selected text is inserted into the composer, as it was before the update.

### Additional information

Installed terminal provenance: SHA-256 of `/home/ei-grad/.local/libexec/shitty` is `c302a2543dae5979adb26619362477315a9a1c0b2c5b5dba66c895eb4002caa9`, identical to the `st` member of release 15's `st-linux-x86_64.tar.gz`. `gh attestation verify` succeeded for that archive against `pg83/shitty`, with signer `https://github.com/pg83/shitty/.github/workflows/release.yml@refs/heads/master`. The archive digest is `2fbeb73f3a88165ce10bab2880b42beb38de61d2f666a0079f7710bdbeea96a1`. The installed file was last modified on 2026-09-02.

The local `[tui]` configuration does not set `fullscreen_transcript`. PR #47178 changed its default to `true` in 0.157.0. In the resulting owned alternate-screen mode, `OverlayInput::Default` captures the mouse; `AlternateScreen::configure_input` enables terminal mouse reporting (`?1000`, `?1002`, `?1006`, `?1003`). The terminal's source confirms the consequence: with mouse reporting active, `VtermInput::pointerButton` sends the button event to the application and returns before reaching its middle-button `paste(true)` branch. `MouseFrontendState::protocolActive` makes Shift bypass mouse reporting. Thus Codex's new default, rather than a change in `shitty`, diverts an unmodified middle click from `shitty`'s native Wayland primary-selection paste path. Sources: https://github.com/openai/codex/pull/47178, https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.157.0/codex-rs/tui/src/tui/alternate_screen.rs, https://github.com/pg83/shitty/blob/bfe3b41cd980b425a8e30263c69d110054f09ff6/lib/shitty/vterm.cpp, and https://github.com/pg83/shitty/blob/bfe3b41cd980b425a8e30263c69d110054f09ff6/lib/shitty/mouse_frontend.cpp.

An explicit `-c tui.fullscreen_transcript=false`, `--no-alt-screen`, or Shift+middle-click may be a temporary workaround; none has yet been verified by a click test. A useful fix would preserve middle-click primary-selection paste while fullscreen transcript is active.

---

items.body:
### What version of Codex is running?
Codex Desktop on Windows 11; bundled MCP client reports `codex-mcp-client/0.155.0-alpha.16.4`.

### What issue are you seeing?
Codex repeatedly sends requests to several enabled remote MCP servers during app startup/reinitialization and attempts OAuth protected-resource discovery, even though these entries are configured with endpoint credentials and no OAuth flow.

The requests are visible in the servers' access logs with the Codex MCP client user agent. Codex logs show protected-resource metadata mismatches: the configured endpoint includes a secret-bearing final path segment, while the metadata advertises a different resource path. The same mismatch repeats across multiple configured servers after restarting Codex.

This creates avoidable traffic against production services. On constrained shared hosting, repeated PHP-backed requests can contribute to database connection pressure. The local evidence confirms repeated HTTP requests and metadata errors; it does not by itself quantify MySQL sessions.

### Sanitized setup
Multiple enabled remote MCP entries use endpoint-specific credentials embedded in the URL path, conceptually:

```toml
[mcp_servers.server]
url = "https://example.invalid/mcp/<redacted-secret>"
```

No OAuth credentials or OAuth login are configured for these entries. This is one observed configuration pattern, not a claim about a specific MCP server implementation.

### Observed behavior
After restarting Codex, within about one minute, each of five enabled remote MCP entries produced repeated protected-resource metadata mismatch warnings in the local Codex logs. The servers' access logs show requests to both the configured MCP endpoint and paths under `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/`, with the Codex MCP client user agent. This was observed outside the configured automation schedules.

A related but different issue is #37387, where `oauth_resource` is ignored for MCP URLs containing query parameters. This report concerns repeated automatic startup discovery/probing for configured remote MCP servers that do not use OAuth.

### Expected behavior
Codex should respect the configured authentication mode and avoid repeatedly initiating OAuth protected-resource discovery for MCP entries that do not use OAuth. If discovery is needed to determine the authentication mode, cache successful and negative results and apply bounded backoff so restarts or retries do not create repeated traffic to every configured server.

Please consider an explicit supported no-OAuth authentication mode, or another way to disable OAuth discovery while retaining on-demand MCP tool use.

### Impact and evidence limits
The observed HTTP traffic is real and appears in the server access logs. Repeated application requests can contribute to load, but I have not captured a simultaneous database process list proving that these requests alone caused connection-slot saturation.

items.title: MCP StreamableHttp: OAuth is attempted when static auth uses a non-Authorization header

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: auth
labels.description: Issues related to authentication and accounts

labels.name: mcp
labels.description: Issues related to the use of model context protocol (MCP) servers

items.body:
## Summary

When an MCP StreamableHttp server is configured with a static auth header that is **not** `Authorization` (for example `x-api-key`), Codex still attempts the OAuth handshake and the connection fails, even though a valid static credential was supplied.

## Where

In `codex-rs/rmcp-client/src/rmcp_client.rs`, the OAuth `auth_provider` is suppressed only when the request carries an `Authorization` header:

```rust
let auth_provider =
    if bearer_token.is_some() || default_headers.contains_key(AUTHORIZATION) {
        None
    } else {
        auth_provider.clone()
    };
```

`build_default_headers` correctly attaches every `http_headers` / `env_http_headers` entry (including a non-`Authorization` header), but because the check keys on `AUTHORIZATION` specifically, a server authenticated purely by `x-api-key` keeps its OAuth `auth_provider` and triggers an OAuth flow.

## Reproduce

Configure a StreamableHttp MCP server whose only auth is a custom header:

```
mcp_servers.example.url = "https://mcp.example.com"
mcp_servers.example.env_http_headers."x-api-key" = "EXAMPLE_KEY_ENV"
```

with `EXAMPLE_KEY_ENV` set to a valid key, against a server that uses `x-api-key` and offers no OAuth. Codex attempts OAuth and the connection fails; the server reports a missing `Authorization` header.

## Expected

Any configured static auth header — via `http_headers` or `env_http_headers`, not only `Authorization` — should suppress the OAuth path. A server may legitimately authenticate with `x-api-key`, `X-Api-Token`, or similar.

## Version

Observed in 0.144.1; the same condition is present on the latest tag.

items.body:
### Codex version

Codex App 26.915.4065.0; managed app-server daemon 0.157.0.

### Platform

Windows 11 Pro, build 26200.

### What happens

Sending a message in a Git repository opens several short-lived Windows Terminal windows. Their tab titles show `git.exe`. A process trace captured four new `OpenConsole.exe` instances at a turn start. The Codex app-server daemon launched Git metadata and status commands including `rev-parse HEAD`, `remote -v`, and `status --porcelain`.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open Codex App in a Git repository on Windows with Windows Terminal set as the default terminal application.
2. Send a message to start a turn.
3. Watch for transient Git terminal windows during turn startup.

### Expected behavior

Background Git checks should run without creating or focusing terminal windows.

### Root cause and proposed fix

`codex-rs/git-utils/src/git_process.rs` starts these commands through `JobObject::spawn_contained`. On Windows, the job-object spawn sets `CREATE_SUSPENDED` but does not set `CREATE_NO_WINDOW`. Its fallback clears creation flags to zero, so that path can also open a console.

Proposed fix: [JRBusiness/codex@67858bd](https://github.com/JRBusiness/codex/commit/67858bd2a4f938391fef42053ef58312a4af74bc). It combines `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` with the suspended job-object spawn and retains the no-window flag in the fallback. This is a fork commit because the repository's contribution policy does not accept external pull requests.

### Verification

- A local Windows launcher using `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` ran the same turn-start Git checks with zero new `OpenConsole.exe` or Windows Terminal processes in the watcher. The upstream patch itself has not been deployed in the Codex App.
- `just fmt` passed on the proposed patch.
- `just test -p codex-git-utils -p codex-utils-pty` passed: 63 tests on Windows.

Related: #24910 and #30345.

Summary
After Codex app-server 0.157.0-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc was installed (through Orca), starting the daemon opens one visible console window per stdio MCP server whose command is npx (a .cmd shim). The same config.toml ran for a week on the previous version without any windows.

Environment
Windows 11 Home 10.0.26200
Codex app-server 0.157.0-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc, launched by Orca as codex.exe app-server --listen unix:// --managed-daemon
Default terminal application: Windows Terminal 1.24.11911.0
Node.js with npx at C:\Program Files\nodejs\npx.cmd
Timeline (local time, 2026-09-25)
08:52:29 — the 0.157.0 release directory was created (auto-update)
08:54:18 — the daemon started 8 stdio MCP servers, and 11 OpenConsole.exe -Embedding processes (Windows Terminal windows) appeared in the same second
The same MCP servers had been configured and in use since 2026-09-18 with no visible windows
Config that reproduces it
TOML
Copy
[mcp_servers.hostinger-vps]
command = "npx"
args = ["--package=hostinger-api-mcp@latest", "hostinger-vps-mcp"]
(I had 8 servers like this.)

Observed process chain (one of the 8)
Copy
codex.exe app-server --managed-daemon
 └─ cmd.exe /e:ON /v:OFF /d /c ""C:\Program Files\nodejs\npx.cmd" "--package=hostinger-api-mcp@latest" hostinger-vps-mcp"
     ├─ conhost.exe 0x4
     └─ node.exe npx-cli.js ...
         └─ cmd.exe /d /s /c hostinger-vps-mcp
             └─ node.exe ...\hostinger-api-mcp\src\servers\vps.js
Every window was titled C:\WINDOWS\system32\cmd.exe, and each was hosted by WindowsTerminal.exe -Embedding.

Not affected
MCP servers whose command is an .exe launched directly (for example node.exe script.js, node_repl.exe) did not open windows. A plugin script that ran through cmd.exe (codex-security) opened one as well.

Expected
Stdio MCP servers start hidden, as they did on the previous version. The daemon has no console of its own, so I think it needs to create child processes with CREATE_NO_WINDOW (or an equivalent hidden startup). Otherwise every console-subsystem child, such as the cmd.exe that runs .cmd shims, gets its own new console. With Windows Terminal as the default terminal, each new console opens as a visible window.

Workaround
Remove the npx-based servers from config.toml, or point command at node.exe with the package’s JS entry point.

items.title: Voice should disclose when it changes the selected model or capability path

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

items.body:
## Summary

When a user starts Voice inside an existing ChatGPT/Codex conversation, the UI strongly suggests that they are continuing the same conversation with the same selected model and capability level, only using speech instead of typing.

That mental model can be wrong.

Voice may introduce a realtime voice model / routing layer, different reasoning behavior, different delegation behavior, or different effective model settings. A user who selected a strong reasoning model such as GPT-5.6 Sol with High reasoning can reasonably assume that switching to Voice preserves the same model/capability path unless the product explicitly says otherwise.

For casual conversation this may not matter much. For engineering, coding, research, architecture, debugging, or other long-running technical work, it can matter a lot.

## User impact

The risky case is not that Voice is "bad". The problem is **silent capability-path substitution**.

Example:

1. A user works for hours in a technical project using a selected reasoning model.
2. They need their hands free and switch to Voice in the same thread.
3. The same thread, context, project, and UI remain visible.
4. The user naturally assumes only the input/output modality changed.
5. In reality, Voice may use a different realtime model or routing path and may not behave identically to the selected chat model/reasoning level.
6. The user continues making design decisions, implementation changes, or research conclusions under the assumption that the same model is still doing the work.
7. They may only discover much later that quality, instruction-following, reasoning depth, or model settings were different.

The user should not have to infer this from differences in model behavior.

## Expected behavior

When Voice does **not** preserve the selected model/capability path one-to-one, the product should disclose that clearly at the moment Voice starts.

For example:

> Voice uses a realtime model and may not behave identically to your selected GPT-5.6 Sol / High configuration.

The UI should also make the active execution path visible during the session, e.g.:

- Voice frontend: GPT-Live / realtime
- Reasoning backend: selected model, if delegated
- Effective reasoning level
- Whether the selected chat model is being used directly, indirectly, or not at all

## Requested improvement

Please consider two complementary changes:

1. **Transparency**
   - Clearly disclose when starting Voice changes the active model, reasoning effort, routing path, tool availability, or other capabilities.
   - Do not make the user infer this from degraded or different behavior.

2. **Voice-as-I/O mode**
   - Add an option where Voice is only the speech interface:
   - audio → end-of-speech detection → transcription → normal prompt in the current thread → selected model/reasoning level produces the answer → TTS output.
   - This would allow hands-free work while preserving the exact selected model, context, tools, and reasoning configuration.

This should be a user choice:
- **Realtime Voice** for maximum conversational responsiveness.
- **Preserve selected model** for maximum continuity and reasoning fidelity.

## Why this matters

The UI currently encourages a reasonable but potentially false assumption:

> "I am still talking to the same AI in the same thread; I only switched from keyboard to microphone."

If that is not technically true, the product should say so explicitly.

For professional or engineering workflows, model identity and reasoning level are part of the execution contract, not an implementation detail.

## Related issues

- #41727 — Voice can silently reset GPT-5.6 Sol High to Low.
- #47396 — Request for continuous dictation where the selected model remains the responder.
- #44131 — Request to keep the selected provider/model/context/tools while using Voice.
- #47754 — Demonstrates a separate voice/backend delegation path in current Voice behavior.

These issues cover parts of the problem. This request focuses specifically on **user-facing transparency and preserving informed consent when Voice changes the effective model/capability path**.

## Environment

Observed in ChatGPT Voice on a paid plan while continuing an existing technical conversation. The concern is product-level rather than a single-platform rendering bug.

No private conversation contents, account identifiers, or logs are included in this report.

items.body:
# [Linux/Hyprland] Pet overlay is 2129 px tall and draws an oversized transparent window

## Summary

With the desktop pet enabled on Linux under Hyprland, the pet's native overlay window is much larger than the visible mascot. On a 1920×1080 display, the measured window is 1128×2129 px. Its transparent area extends over most of the screen, and Hyprland decorations (border, shadow, and blur) make the oversized bounds especially visible. The same outer dimensions were observed with both XWayland and native Wayland rendering.

This appears to be an upstream overlay geometry problem, rather than only a Hyprland decoration rule: removing border, shadow, and blur changes the appearance but does not change the window geometry.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Run the ChatGPT desktop app on Linux in a Hyprland session with a 1920×1080 display.
2. Enable or wake the desktop pet.
3. Inspect the pet overlay's native window bounds in Hyprland, first with the default XWayland launcher and then with native Wayland enabled.
4. Observe that the overlay measures 1128×2129 px in both modes although the visible pet is small.

## Expected behavior

The overlay's native bounds should track the visible pet and its controls, with only the necessary transparent padding. On a 1080p display, the overlay should not extend to 2129 px tall or span 1128 px horizontally for a small pet.

## Actual behavior

The overlay window measures 1128×2129 px on a 1920×1080 display. Most of that area is transparent. Hyprland applies its normal border/shadow/blur treatment to the full native bounds, making the invisible excess area apparent and potentially affecting window rules and interactions.

## Environment and diagnostics

- OS: Linux (Arch Linux)
- Compositor: Hyprland
- Display: 1920×1080; both attached displays report 1080 px height
- App: ChatGPT desktop Linux preview, package `chatgpt-bin 26.917.71314-1` (local Arch package metadata)
- Launch backends checked: default XWayland and native Wayland
- Pet overlay measured at 1128×2129 px in both backends
- In XWayland, the idle pet input shape was one 80×87 px rectangle.
- A local, read-only inspection of `/usr/lib/chatgpt/resources/app.asar` found the minified native pet layout function computes vertical drawing bounds from the maximum of the display height and anchor height, then adds 28 px of padding above and below. `getLayoutForDisplay` supplies the tallest display height. With a 1080 px display and 87 px anchor, this yields 2129 px of native window height. This is a static interpretation of the packaged bundle, not a source-level diagnosis. The measured 1128 px width is reported as observed; its precise calculation has not been established.
- Existing local Hyprland rules remove border, shadow, and blur from the pet window; those rules do not reduce its native bounds.

## Forced-size experiment

As a temporary diagnostic, the live Hyprland Lua dispatcher resized the pet window from `1128×2129` to `480×720`. Hyprland then reported the resized window at `[1310,1620]`, compared with its original position `[986,915]`. In a captured screenshot, the pet and controls were not visible on either display. This shows that the forced bounds did not yield a verified usable pet, but does not establish whether it was moved or clipped. After restoring the original geometry, the pet and controls were visible again near the lower-right of the main monitor. No persistent resize rule was installed. Screenshots are available on request.

## Workaround

Disable or tuck away the pet when the oversized transparent window is disruptive. Hyprland rules can suppress its border, shadow, and blur, but do not correct the window size.

## Related reports checked

No exact public Linux/Hyprland report matching these measurements was found in the OpenAI Codex issue tracker or OpenAI developer community search. These are related overlay reports, but they describe different symptoms/platforms:

- [#41596: Windows transparent overlay captures a large screen area and pet cannot be dragged](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/41596) — Windows-only; large-area input capture rather than Linux oversized native geometry.
- [#41501: Windows pet overlay loses its hit region after the first drag](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/41501) — Windows input-region failure; its discussion independently notes a fixed approximately 772×2129 transparent canvas, but the reported failure is Windows-specific.
- [#21230: Codex pet overlay is cropped inside its floating container](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/21230) — macOS clipping, not an oversized Linux window.
- [OpenAI Developer Community: Codex in ChatGPT desktop app for Linux is now in preview](https://community.openai.com/t/codex-in-chatgpt-desktop-app-for-linux-is-now-in-preview/1390027) — general Linux preview discussion; no exact geometry match found.

## Request

Please size and position the Linux native overlay from the visible pet/control bounds (plus modest padding), or otherwise constrain its native geometry so a display-height-based transparent canvas does not extend beyond the screen. Please verify the resulting native window bounds on both XWayland and native Wayland under Hyprland.

## Caveat

The geometry measurements, forced-size experiment, and bundle inspection are local observations. XWayland's input shape was inspected; native Wayland's input region was not independently inspected. The matching outer dimensions across the two rendering modes were measured, but the bundle explanation is a static reading of a minified packaged function and should be confirmed by maintainers against source.

items.body:
### What version of the IDE extension are you using?

`openai.chatgpt-26.917.62051-win32-x64`

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT Pro 20x, using ChatGPT account sign-in.

### Which IDE are you using?

Visual Studio Code.

### What platform is your computer?

Windows x64; reported OS version `10.0.26200.0`.

### What issue are you seeing?

The `Work locally` dropdown does not show `Usage remaining`, and the extension's Status panel shows `Rate limit: Unavailable`. Context usage is still displayed normally.

The web usage dashboard works for the affected account. Reloading the VS Code window and signing out/in did not resolve it. Switching to other accounts in the same extension installation shows usage normally.

Runtime diagnostics and inspection of the installed extension identify a mismatch between the extension-host `account-info` response and the webview's authenticated user identity. The affected account uses the SSE usage transport. Its usage HTTP request succeeds, but the webview rejects the response because its expected authenticated user ID is null.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Use the extension version above on Windows and sign in with an account for which the usage transport is `sse`.
2. Open a local conversation and expand `Work locally`.
3. Open the Status panel.
4. Observe that usage is missing from the dropdown and Status reports `Rate limit: Unavailable`, despite the web usage dashboard showing data.
5. Reload the window or sign in again: the symptom persists.

The transport setting is account-dependent; this report does not assume every Pro account is assigned SSE.

### What is the expected behavior?

Valid usage data for the signed-in user should populate the remaining-usage UI. The extension host and webview should agree on the authenticated identity fields, including when SSE usage updates are enabled.

### Additional information

#### Runtime evidence

Temporary diagnostic logging was added only to record response status, field-presence booleans, identity-match booleans, and rate-window metadata. Three consecutive requests on September 25, 2026 produced this pattern:

```text
HTTP:
  httpStatus=200
  accountMatchesRequest=true
  hasAccountId=true
  hasUserId=true
  planType=pro
  primaryPresent=true
  primaryWindowSeconds=604800

Webview usage query:
  transport=sse
  nullResponse=false
  accountMatches=true
  expectedAccountPresent=true
  expectedUserPresent=false
  userMatches=false
  primaryPresent=true
  primaryWindowSeconds=604800
```

The bundled app server's `account/rateLimits/read` also returned valid rate-limit data. This is not an empty server-side allowance response.

#### Field mismatch in the installed extension

- In `out/extension.js`, the successful `account-info` handler returns `accountId`, `userId`, `plan`, `email`, `computeResidency`, and `hasChatGptToken`. It does **not** return `authenticatedUserId`. Its existing `userId` comes from the authenticated token's `chatgpt_user_id`.
- In `webview/assets/app-initial-e47a6bae212d.js`, `kEi` selects `accountInfo.authenticatedUserId ?? null` when the account IDs match and stores that as the webview's authenticated user identity.
- In `webview/assets/app-initial-de4359f78ed1.js`, the usage-query logic checks the response's `user_id` against that identity when the transport is `sse`. A mismatch cancels the query and throws a silent cancellation.
- Here, the response contains a valid user ID but the expected ID is null, so the successful response is discarded. The usage-window display consequently has no usable data.

Simplified equivalent of the relevant logic:

```js
// Extension host: authenticatedUserId is absent.
const accountInfo = { accountId, userId /* other fields */ };

// Webview identity selection:
const expectedUserId =
  accountInfo.accountId === authenticatedAccountId
    ? accountInfo.authenticatedUserId ?? null
    : null;

// Usage query, after HTTP 200:
if (
  transport === "sse" &&
  response != null &&
  response.user_id !== expectedUserId
) {
  // Cancel the query with a silent cancellation.
}
```

#### Controlled reproduction

The account-info return expression, frontend identity-selection expression, and usage rejection condition were extracted from the installed JavaScript and evaluated locally with synthetic identities:

| Case | Response rejected by the identity condition? |
| --- | --- |
| Existing account-info fields + SSE | Yes |
| Existing account-info fields + polling | No |
| Same response with authenticatedUserId populated from the existing authenticated userId + SSE | No |

The affected account's SSE selection was observed directly. Other accounts were not each instrumented, so polling is a code-supported explanation for the account-dependent behavior, rather than a claim about every working account.

#### Suggested fix direction

Populate `authenticatedUserId` in the extension host's `account-info` contract using the same authenticated source as its existing `userId`, or otherwise align the producer and consumer contracts while preserving identity checks. Add coverage for the VS Code bridge with SSE usage enabled.

This proposed field completion passed the local expression-level comparison; it has **not** been applied and verified as an end-to-end UI fix.

Temporary diagnostic modifications were removed after investigation, and restored files were checked against their original hashes. No account IDs, user IDs, email addresses, credentials, private filesystem paths, or full session transcripts are included in this report.
